name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to automate messaging, channel and conversation reads, user lookups, and workspace queries. Use when Gemini CLI needs to send or manage Slack messages, fetch channel history or members, respond to Slack events, or build Slack bots and integrations with bot/user tokens.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Perform Slack Web API operations directly over HTTPS (`https://slack.com/api/<method>`) with an OAuth token. Every response is JSON with `"ok": true|false`; on failure an `error` string explains why. Do not invent API methods — verify against the official Slack Web API docs (https://api.slack.com/methods) when a method is unfamiliar.

## Authentication

- Send the token in an HTTP header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (preferred over the deprecated `token` form parameter).
- Bot tokens start with `xoxb-`; user tokens with `xoxp-`. Never hardcode tokens — read `SLACK_TOKEN` from the environment or a user-provided secret.
- Before a workflow, validate the token once with `auth.test`; it returns the bot/user identity and workspace. Failure here means invalid credentials — stop and report instead of retrying every call.
- Permission is scope-based. Missing scope errors (`missing_scope`, `not_allowed`) mean the token lacks required scopes; report the exact scope needed, e.g. `chat:write`, `channels:history`, `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `users:read`.

## Quick Start: Send a Message

POST JSON to `chat.postMessage` to send a message to a channel or DM:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello from Gemini CLI!"}'
```

Expected success payload (report these IDs to the user):

```json
{ "ok": true, "channel": "C1234567890", "ts": "1717000000.000000" }
```

`ts` is the message timestamp and is the permanent identifier used to update, delete, or thread a message. Plain `text` supports Slack formatting: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `:emoji:`, `<https://example.com|label>` links, and `<@U123>` / `<!channel>` mentions.

## Common Workflows

### 1. Send messages (task-based)

- **Plain message**: `chat.postMessage` with `channel` + `text`.
- **Rich message**: pass a `blocks` array (Block Kit, https://api.slack.com/block-kit) with `"type":"section"` / `"type":"divider"` / `"type":"actions"` entries; when `blocks` is present, keep `text` as a short plain-text fallback for notifications and accessibility.
- **Thread reply**: add `"thread_ts": "<parent ts>"` to reply inside a thread.
- **DM a user**: call `conversations.open` with `{"users":"U123"}` to obtain the DM channel id, then `chat.postMessage` to that channel.
- **Ephemeral message**: `chat.postEphemeral` with `channel` + `user` shows a message only to that user.
- **Update / delete**: `chat.update` (`channel`, `ts`, new `text`/`blocks`) or `chat.delete` (`channel`, `ts`). Only the message author may modify or delete.
- **Scheduling**: `chat.scheduleMessage` (`post_at` as a Unix timestamp) then `chat.deleteScheduledMessage` with the returned `scheduled_message_id`.

Text size limit is 40,000 characters (`msg_too_long`); Block Kit `text` fields are limited to 3,000 characters. Prefer truncating long content with a clear notice over dropping it silently.

### 2. Read conversations and history

- `conversations.list` — list channels. Query params: `types=public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim`, `exclude_archived=true`, `limit=200`. Never assume `conversations.list` returns everything — it paginates (see Pagination).
- `conversations.history` — recent messages in a channel: `channel`, `limit` (max 200, most recent first), optional `oldest`/`latest` Unix timestamps to bound the window. Returned messages include `ts`, `user`, `text`, `blocks`, `thread_ts`, and `reactions` when `include_all_metadata` applies.
- `conversations.replies` — fetch an entire thread: `channel` + `ts` of the thread root.
- `conversations.info` — metadata (name, topic, purpose, member count) for one conversation.
- `conversations.members` — list member user ids of a channel; combine with `users.info` to resolve profiles.
- `conversations.join` — join a public channel before posting when the bot is not a member (older channels may instead return `not_in_channel`).

### 3. Find users and workspace info

- `users.list` — all workspace users (paginated; typically called once and cached).
- `users.info` (`user` param) — profile, name, email, timezone for one user.
- `users.lookupByEmail` — resolve `email` → user object directly.
- `users.conversations` — conversations a given user is in.
- `team.info` — workspace name, domain, and id.

## Pagination

List-style methods return at most a page (commonly `limit` up to 200). Follow the cursor pattern instead of assuming a full result:

```bash
curl -sS "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?types=public_channel&limit=200" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"
```

1. Read `response_metadata.next_cursor` from the response.
2. If it is non-empty, repeat the request with `cursor=<next_cursor>`.
3. Accumulate results until `next_cursor` is `""` or absent.

Write a loop (in the caller's language of choice) that stops on `"ok": false` and surfaces the `error`.

## Rate Limits and Errors

- Slack tiers requests per method per workspace/app. On exceeding, the API returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header (seconds) and `"ok": false, "error": "rate_limited"`.
- Back off and retry respecting `Retry-After`; also honor the `Retry-After` on transient 5xx responses. Use exponential backoff with jitter for network failures.
- Handle these common `error` values explicitly:
  - `invalid_auth` / `not_authed` — token missing, malformed, or revoked.
  - `account_inactive` — token's owner deactivated.
  - `channel_not_found` / `not_in_channel` — wrong channel id or bot must join first.
  - `is_archived` — cannot post to an archived channel.
  - `missing_scope` / `not_allowed` — token lacks the required OAuth scope.
  - `msg_too_long` / `invalid_blocks` — payload validation failure.
- Always check `ok` before trusting payload fields; report the `error` verbatim to the user with the offending method and parameters.

## Guidance for Automation Scripts

- Suppress stack traces; print concise success lines, e.g. `Success: message ts=1717000000.000000 sent to #general`.
- Truncate long JSON payloads in output (first ~50 lines) to protect the context window.
- When repeatedly sending files, check current docs for the two-step external upload flow (`files.getUploadURLExternal` + `files.completeUploadExternal`) before falling back to legacy `files.upload`; upload methods may require additional scopes.

## Verification and Cleanup

- After sending, confirm `"ok": true` and echo the `channel` + `ts`.
- Do not post test messages to real channels without user consent; prefer a dedicated sandbox channel or `chat.postEphemeral` against the requesting user.
- After a failure, never retry blindly when the error is authorization- or payload-related — fix the token or payload first.
